stem: Kabir must solve $6x + 8 = 26$ by isolating $x$. The two sides are already equal.

parts.text: Which first move preserves equality and removes the unwanted $+8$?

options.text: Subtract $8$ from the left side only, writing $6x = 26$.
The first move is the label "inverse operations".
Take $x = 26$, because $26$ is the largest printed number.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The sides stay equal when the same subtraction is done on both; subtracting $8$ from each side removes the unwanted $+8$ and leaves $6x = 18$.

teacher.key_rationale: Same operation on both sides preserves equality. Subtracting 8 from both sides isolates the 6x term: 6x=18. B drops the both-sides condition. C substitutes the topic label. D grabs the largest printed number.
